column2: Check the image path, signature, parent process and network connections; hash the binary and look it up before ending the process.
Find who created the entry and when, hash what it launches, and compare it with a known-good build before removing it.
Confirm a standard user can write to the path or setting; fix the permissions or quote the path, then re-scan to confirm it is gone.
Identify the source host and account, check the matching logon events from the same time, and look for the same tool on other hosts.
Ask the owner whether this remote-management tool is approved; if not, record when and by which account it was installed before removing it.
Ask the user whether they ran it; check where the file came from and when it first appeared.
Decode the script in a safe place without running it; look for download commands, encoded payloads and where the file came from.
Hash the file, check where it came from and when it was created, and compare it with your allowlist before treating it as hostile.
Check where the download came from and whether it was opened or run afterwards.
Compare the entry with what this host is meant to use; unexpected overrides can redirect traffic.
List the source addresses and target accounts in the logon events and check whether any attempt later succeeded.
Confirm the account is expected, who created it and when; set a password or disable the account if it is not needed.
Check whether the log was cleared or stopped on purpose and compare it with a copy forwarded to a collector.
Verify the file against the package manager and confirm it is meant to carry the setuid bit.
Confirm each key belongs to a known person or system and check when authorized_keys last changed.
Read the surrounding commands and timestamps for downloads, credential use and cleanup.
Confirm whether this host is meant to run containers or is inside one; review mounted paths and privileges.
A match from your own indicator list; confirm it is not a coincidence, then search other hosts for the same indicator.
Review the evidence section named in this finding and confirm with the owner whether it is expected.
